title: Pre-Qin Literature
full_title: Pre-Qin Literature: From Myth to the Masters
tagline: Myths, the *Book of Songs*, its forms and techniques, historical prose, narrative in the *Zuo Zhuan*, the *Analects* and the *Mencius*, Zhuangzi and the other Masters, Qu Yuan and the *Li Sao*, the *Songs of Chu*, and the legacy of early literature
summary: The literature of the centuries before the Qin unification laid foundations that Chinese writers drew on for the next two thousand years. This course reads the early myths, the *Book of Songs*, the historical prose of the *Book of Documents*, the *Zuo Zhuan* and the *Discourses of the States*, the prose of Confucius, Mencius, Zhuangzi and the other Masters, and the poetry of Qu Yuan and the *Songs of Chu*.

chapters.title: Myths
chapters.summary: The fragmentary myths of ancient China — Nüwa, Pangu, Kuafu, Jingwei — where they are recorded, and why they survive only in pieces.

chapters.title: The *Book of Songs*
chapters.summary: The 305 poems, how the anthology was compiled, its Airs, Odes and Hymns, and how it became a Confucian classic.

chapters.title: Form and technique in the *Book of Songs*
chapters.summary: Four-character lines, repetition across stanzas, and the techniques of *fu*, *bi* and *xing*.

chapters.title: Historical prose
chapters.summary: The *Book of Documents*, the *Spring and Autumn Annals*, the *Zuo Zhuan*, the *Discourses of the States* and the *Intrigues of the Warring States*.

chapters.title: Narrative in the *Zuo Zhuan*
chapters.summary: How the *Zuo Zhuan* tells of battles, speeches and people, and its influence on later historical writing.

chapters.title: The *Analects* and the *Mencius*
chapters.summary: Recorded sayings and argument: the style of the *Analects* and the persuasive prose of Mencius.

chapters.title: Zhuangzi and the other Masters
chapters.summary: The parables of Zhuangzi, the essays of Xunzi and Han Feizi, and the Mohists and other schools as literature.

chapters.title: Qu Yuan and the *Li Sao*
chapters.summary: Qu Yuan’s life and the *Li Sao*: its fragrant plants and fair ones, its journeys among the gods, and its place in Chinese culture.

chapters.title: The *Songs of Chu*
chapters.summary: The *Nine Songs*, the *Heavenly Questions* and other pieces, the culture of Chu, and how the *Chuci* differ from the *Book of Songs*.

chapters.title: The legacy of pre-Qin literature
chapters.summary: The *Book of Songs* and the *Songs of Chu* as the two sources of Chinese poetry, the traditions of prose founded in this period, and how later writers read them.
